GENERAL SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin Lenses ● Types of lenses ● Properties of thin lenses (principal focus, opti.

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.

5. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.

   C. Guess results without recording observations on Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts ? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .

10. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.

12. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Milk souring

13. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature? (1 mark)

   D. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature.

15. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Reproduction? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Reproduction.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Reproduction.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproduction.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Human Reproduction.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Uniform Circular motion ● Terms used in uniform circular motion (radian, angular and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Heating effect of current ● Experiments on heating effect of current ● Factors d and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Human Reproduction and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
